question: Which term is used to describe a freely movable joint in the body?
explanation: Diarthroses are synovial joints that permit a wide range of free movements necessary for limb mobility. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why is the pubic symphysis classified as an amphiarthrosis?

options.A: It is tightly fused by bone with no movement at all
options.B: It allows very little movement to provide stability
options.C: It permits completely free movement during childbirth
options.D: It contains a fluid-filled cavity for rapid rotation

explanation: Amphiarthroses provide slight movement combined with high structural stability, typical of the pubic symphysis. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which type of joint features a fluid-filled cavity?
explanation: Synovial joints are uniquely characterized by the presence of a fluid-filled synovial cavity separating articulating bones. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h2)

question: A patient has an injury to a joint that lacks a joint cavity and is held tightly by collagen fibers. What type of joint is this?
explanation: Fibrous joints are bound by dense collagen fibers and do not possess a joint cavity. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the main job of synovial fluid inside a joint?

options.A: Producing red blood cells for the joint
options.B: Sensing pain and deep pressure changes
options.D: Anchoring skeletal muscle directly to bone

explanation: Synovial fluid lubricates articulating surfaces and provides vital nutrients to avascular articular cartilage. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h3)

question: A patient has pain and swelling in the fluid-filled sac over the kneecap. Which structure is inflamed?
explanation: Bursae are synovial sacs that cushion areas of high friction, such as tendons moving over bony prominences. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which movement decreases the angle between two bones?
explanation: Flexion is an angular movement that reduces the angle between bones, bringing them closer together. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the term for moving a limb away from the midline of the body?
explanation: Abduction moves a body part away from the median plane, while adduction brings it toward the midline. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which synovial joint type allows movement in all directions, including rotation?
explanation: Ball-and-socket joints possess a spherical head and cup socket, providing the widest range of multiaxial movement. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which joint allows you to turn your head from side to side?
explanation: Pivot joints consist of a rounded bone fitting into a ring, specialized for uniaxial rotation like shaking the head. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h5)

question: What provides the most important support and stability for many joints?
explanation: Low-level contraction of muscles spanning a joint provides continuous dynamic stability, especially in weight-bearing areas. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h6)

question: How do bone shape and joint movement generally relate to each other?

options.A: Mobility and stability increase at the exact same rate
options.B: Deep socket joints always allow the widest range of movement
options.C: Greater bone interlocking reduces total range of motion
options.D: Ligaments replace the need for articular surfaces entirely

explanation: Deep, well-fitted articular surfaces increase stability but physically limit the range of motion available. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the main cause of gouty arthritis?

options.C: Uric acid crystal deposition in joints

explanation: Gout occurs when excess uric acid builds up in the blood and forms needle-like crystals in joint spaces. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h7)

question: How is rheumatoid arthritis different from osteoarthritis?

options.A: Osteoarthritis involves systemic destruction of organ tissues
options.B: Rheumatoid arthritis is an inflammatory autoimmune disease
options.C: Osteoarthritis is caused by sudden bacterial infections
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis only affects the joints of the fingers

explanation: RA is systemic and autoimmune, whereas OA is primarily a degenerative wear-and-tear condition of articular cartilage. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h7)
